<h1>dropper.exe</h1>
<p>PE32+ executable for Windows (x86-64, console) (high confidence), 37.5 KiB. Risk <strong>58/100 high</strong>.</p>
<p><em>Static analysis only; the file was never executed.</em></p>
<p>Turn on JavaScript to see the interactive report: charts, tables, imports and strings.</p>
<h2>Findings (4)</h2>
<h3><span class="td-sev">high</span> <code>imports.process-injection</code> Imports cover the full process-injection chain (allocate, write, execute)</h3>
<p>Confidence: medium</p>
<h4>Evidence</h4>
<ul>
<li>allocate or map memory in another process: KERNEL32.dll!VirtualAllocEx</li>
<li>write to another process: KERNEL32.dll!WriteProcessMemory</li>
<li>start or hijack a thread there: KERNEL32.dll!CreateRemoteThread</li>
</ul>
<h4>Code</h4>

<h4>Limitations of the code shown</h4>
<ul>
<li>x86 and x86-64 only: other instruction sets are not decoded.</li>
<li>A linear sweep: data inside a code section can be read as instructions, and one wrong byte shifts everything after it.</li>
<li>A view of the code, not a decompilation. Nothing was executed.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Limitations</h4>
<ul>
<li>API presence alone proves nothing: legitimate software (debuggers, installers, security and remote-support tools) imports the same functions.</li>
<li>Functions resolved at run time (GetProcAddress, dlsym) or hidden by a packer are not in the import table, so a missing cluster proves nothing either.</li>
</ul>
